title: John Chapter 21 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 21 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 21 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 21.

questions.question: In John 21, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus showed himself again to the disciples
Simon Peter said he would go fishing
The disciples saw a fire of coals
Jesus asked if they had any meat
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus showed himself again to the disciples
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in John 21:1.

questions.question: Who was with Simon Peter when they went fishing?
options: Thomas, Nathanael, and the sons of Zebedee
questions.correctAnswer: Thomas, Nathanael, and the sons of Zebedee
questions.explanation: This is stated in John 21:2, listing those who were together with Simon Peter.

questions.question: What did Simon Peter say he would do?
questions.explanation: This is explicitly stated in John 21:3 where Simon Peter says, 'I go a fishing.'

questions.question: What did the disciples catch that night?
questions.explanation: John 21:3 states that they went forth and caught nothing that night.

questions.question: Who stood on the shore in the morning?
questions.explanation: According to John 21:4, Jesus stood on the shore when morning came.

questions.question: What did Jesus ask the disciples when he called to them?
questions.explanation: This question is recorded in John 21:5 where Jesus asks the disciples if they have any meat.

questions.question: What did Jesus instruct the disciples to do with their nets?
options: Cast the net on the right side of the ship
questions.correctAnswer: Cast the net on the right side of the ship
questions.explanation: This instruction is found in John 21:6 where Jesus tells them to cast the net on the right side.

questions.question: What did the disciples not have before Jesus spoke to them?
questions.explanation: As noted in John 21:5, the disciples answered that they had no meat.

questions.question: What did the disciple whom Jesus loved say to Peter?
questions.explanation: This statement is made in John 21:7 when that disciple recognizes Jesus.

questions.question: How far were the disciples from land when they were in the little ship?
questions.explanation: John 21:8 specifies that they were not far from land, but as it were two hundred cubits.

questions.question: What did the disciples see when they came to land?
questions.explanation: As stated in John 21:9, they saw a fire of coals when they came to land.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus showed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias.
questions.explanation: This is a true statement found in John 21:1.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples caught a large number of fish before Jesus spoke to them.
questions.explanation: This is true because they caught nothing before Jesus told them to cast the net, according to John 21:3.

questions.question: True or False: Simon Peter was the only disciple present when Jesus spoke to them.
questions.explanation: This is false as multiple disciples were present, as stated in John 21:2.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus asked the disciples if they had any bread.
questions.explanation: This is false; Jesus asked if they had any meat, as recorded in John 21:5.

medium.title: John Chapter 21 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 21 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus ask the disciples to bring to him?
questions.explanation: Jesus asked them to bring of the fish which they had now caught as stated in John 21:10.

questions.question: What does John 21:11 promise will happen if someone brings the fish to Jesus as instructed in John 21:10?
options: They will not break the net
questions.correctAnswer: They will not break the net
questions.explanation: The net was full and yet was not broken, demonstrating the abundance of the catch as mentioned in John 21:11.

questions.question: What did Jesus invite the disciples to do after they had caught the fish?
questions.explanation: Jesus invited them to dine together, as stated in John 21:12.

questions.question: What does John 21:12 indicate about the disciples' recognition of Jesus?
options: They were unsure who he was
They thought he was a stranger
They did not care to ask
questions.correctAnswer: They did not care to ask
questions.explanation: None of the disciples dared to ask who He was, knowing that it was the Lord, as noted in John 21:12.

questions.question: What is significant about the number of fish caught?
options: It was an exact number of 153
It was symbolic of the disciples' faith
questions.correctAnswer: It was an exact number of 153
questions.explanation: The net was drawn full of great fishes, an exact count of 153, as stated in John 21:11.

questions.question: What did Jesus give to the disciples after they dined?
questions.explanation: Jesus took bread and gave it to them, along with fish, as mentioned in John 21:13.

questions.question: How many times did Jesus show himself to his disciples after his resurrection according to John 21:14?
questions.explanation: This event marks the third time Jesus showed himself to his disciples after his resurrection, as stated in John 21:14.

questions.question: What question did Jesus ask Simon Peter to test his love?
options: Do you love me more than these?
questions.correctAnswer: Do you love me more than these?
questions.explanation: Jesus asked Peter if he loved him more than the others, as stated in John 21:15.

questions.question: What command did Jesus give to Peter after affirming his love?
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed Peter to feed his sheep as a response to Peter's declaration of love, mentioned in John 21:15.

questions.question: What was Peter's reaction when Jesus asked him the third time if he loved him?
questions.explanation: Peter was grieved because Jesus asked him the third time, as stated in John 21:17.

questions.question: What does John 21:18 say about Peter's future?
options: He will preach to the nations
He will be taken where he does not want to go
questions.correctAnswer: He will be taken where he does not want to go
questions.explanation: John 21:18 predicts that Peter will stretch forth his hands and be taken where he does not want to go.

questions.question: Jesus' command to Peter to 'Feed my lambs' emphasizes the importance of what aspect of Christian leadership?
questions.explanation: The command emphasizes that true leadership involves caring for and nurturing the followers, as indicated in John 21:15.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus only showed himself to the disciples one time after his resurrection.
questions.explanation: Jesus showed himself to his disciples three times after his resurrection, as stated in John 21:14.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples recognized Jesus immediately when he was on the shore.
questions.explanation: The disciples did not recognize Jesus at first when he stood on the shore, as noted in John 21:4.

questions.question: True or False: Peter was happy when Jesus asked him if he loved him the third time.
questions.explanation: Peter was grieved when Jesus asked him the third time if he loved him, as mentioned in John 21:17.

hard.title: John Chapter 21 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 21.

questions.question: In John 21:19, what did Jesus signify by speaking about the kind of death Peter would glorify God by?
options: Peter would die a martyr's death
Peter would live a long life
Peter would be denied three times
questions.correctAnswer: Peter would die a martyr's death
questions.explanation: John 21:19 states, 'This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God,' indicating Jesus foretold Peter's martyrdom.

questions.question: Who was the disciple that Peter saw following Jesus in John 21:20?
questions.explanation: John 21:20 identifies the follower as 'the disciple whom Jesus loved,' a title used only for John in this Gospel.

questions.question: In John 21:21, what question did Peter ask Jesus about the disciple whom Jesus loved?
options: Lord, and what shall this man do?
Will he live until the end of the age?
questions.correctAnswer: Lord, and what shall this man do?
questions.explanation: John 21:21 records Peter's question as, 'Lord, and what shall this man do?' regarding the beloved disciple's future.

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to Peter's question about the disciple in John 21:22?
options: If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me.
You must tell him what to do.
questions.correctAnswer: If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me.
questions.explanation: John 21:22 records Jesus' response emphasizing Peter’s focus on his own calling rather than the beloved disciple's fate.

questions.question: What misunderstanding spread among the brethren concerning the beloved disciple according to John 21:23?
options: That he would become the leader of the church
That he was not actually a disciple
questions.explanation: John 21:23 explains a saying went abroad that the beloved disciple should not die, clarifying Jesus did not explicitly say this.

questions.question: According to John 21:24, who is the disciple that testifies and wrote these things?
questions.explanation: John 21:24 identifies 'this is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things,' referring to the beloved disciple (traditionally John).

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'tarry' (μείνω) in John 21:22 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek verb 'μείνω' translated as 'tarry' means 'to remain or stay,' as used in John 21:22 in the context of remaining until Jesus comes again.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Jesus' thrice-repeated question to Peter in John 21:15-17?
questions.explanation: The thrice-repeated question 'Lovest thou me?' in John 21:15-17 employs repetition to emphasize restoration and commissioning of Peter.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares a thematic connection with Jesus' charge to Peter to 'Feed my sheep' in John 21:16?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 34:11-16 speaks of God as shepherd caring for His sheep, paralleling Jesus' charge to Peter to shepherd His followers in John 21:16.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Jesus' statement in John 21:18 about Peter's manner of death?
questions.explanation: Acts 12:2 records the martyrdom of James by the sword, reflecting the theme of apostolic martyrdom as foretold to Peter in John 21:18-19.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus' question to Peter 'Lovest thou me?' in John 21:15?
options: The disciples eating breakfast on the shore
Jesus' resurrection appearance to the women
The healing of the blind man
questions.correctAnswer: The disciples eating breakfast on the shore
questions.explanation: John 21:12-14 describes Jesus preparing and sharing breakfast with the disciples on the shore immediately before questioning Peter in verse 15.

questions.question: How does John 21:25 employ literary hyperbole to express the scope of Jesus' works?
options: Saying the world could not contain the books if all were written
Claiming Jesus performed only a few miracles
Describing Jesus as an ordinary man
questions.correctAnswer: Saying the world could not contain the books if all were written
questions.explanation: John 21:25 uses hyperbole stating the whole world could not contain the books if all Jesus' deeds were recorded, emphasizing His vast works.

questions.question: What typological significance does Peter casting himself into the sea in John 21:7 have in the broader biblical narrative?
options: Symbolizes dying to old self to follow Christ
Represents a literal baptism by water
questions.correctAnswer: Symbolizes dying to old self to follow Christ
questions.explanation: Peter casting himself into the sea (John 21:7) typologically parallels dying to old life and being reborn as a follower, echoing baptismal imagery.

questions.question: How does the phrase 'Follow me' in John 21:19 and 21:22 function as an inclusio in the chapter?
options: It frames Peter's restoration and mission
It signals the end of the narrative
It quotes an Old Testament prophet
questions.correctAnswer: It frames Peter's restoration and mission
questions.explanation: The repeated command 'Follow me' at John 21:19 and 21:22 forms an inclusio framing the call for Peter's restoration and Christian mission.

questions.question: True or False: John 21:24 confirms that the testimony of the disciple who wrote the Gospel is considered true by the community.
questions.explanation: John 21:24 states, 'and we know that his testimony is true,' affirming the authenticity and acceptance of the beloved disciple's witness.

theological.title: John Chapter 21 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 21 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 21:6 teach about God's provision and sovereignty in salvation?
options: God sovereignly provides abundantly beyond human effort
God only provides material needs, not spiritual ones
God expects humans to provide for themselves without divine aid
God's provision is always limited and conditional upon perfect obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly provides abundantly beyond human effort
questions.explanation: John 21:6 shows Jesus directing the disciples to cast their net on the right side, resulting in a miraculous catch of fish, illustrating God's sovereign provision beyond human capacity.

questions.question: What doctrine about Christ's resurrection appearance and its purpose is taught in John 21:14?
options: Christ's resurrection appearances confirm His victory over death and assure believers
Resurrection appearances were symbolic visions rather than physical events
The resurrection appearances were limited to only one time and one place
The resurrection appearances were meant primarily to establish a new law
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's resurrection appearances confirm His victory over death and assure believers
questions.explanation: John 21:14 states this is the third time Jesus showed himself to His disciples after rising, indicating the reality and purpose of His resurrection appearances to confirm His victory and reassure them.

questions.question: What doctrine about pastoral responsibility and love is taught in John 21:15?
options: True pastoral leadership is based on love and caring for Christ’s lambs
Pastoral leadership depends solely on authority and discipline
Love is unrelated to the task of feeding Christ’s sheep
Pastoral care is a temporary responsibility limited to the early church
questions.correctAnswer: True pastoral leadership is based on love and caring for Christ’s lambs
questions.explanation: John 21:15 commands Peter to feed Jesus’ lambs after affirming his love, linking pastoral duty directly to love for Christ and His people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 21:5 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In John 21:5 Jesus asks if they have any meat, knowing their situation perfectly, demonstrating His divine omniscience about their needs.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly demonstrated in John 21:18 where Jesus predicts Peter’s death?
questions.explanation: Jesus' detailed prophecy about Peter’s death in John 21:18 reveals His foreknowledge of future events.

questions.question: How does John 21:11 connect to Old Testament themes of God’s provision and covenant faithfulness?
options: It echoes God’s covenant faithfulness by providing abundantly, reminiscent of manna provision
It contradicts Old Testament provision by focusing on human effort
It diminishes God’s role by emphasizing the net’s strength
It highlights Israel’s failure to catch fish as a sign of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes God’s covenant faithfulness by providing abundantly, reminiscent of manna provision
questions.explanation: The great catch of 153 fish in John 21:11 symbolizes God’s abundant and faithful provision, similar to manna provision in the wilderness, fulfilling covenant promises.

questions.question: How does John 21:22 relate to the broader New Testament teaching on discipleship and individual responsibility?
options: It emphasizes following Christ personally without comparing one’s path to others
It teaches that all disciples will have the same ministry and destiny
It suggests that discipleship depends on knowing others’ destinies
It promotes indifference to personal discipleship
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes following Christ personally without comparing one’s path to others
questions.explanation: In John 21:22, Jesus instructs Peter to focus on his own calling rather than the fate of another disciple, highlighting individual responsibility in discipleship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 21:15 and John 21:17 teach about pastoral ministry and restoration?
options: Pastoral ministry requires love and involves restoration after failure
Pastoral ministry is based on strict judgment without restoration
Love is irrelevant to pastoral duties
Restoration is unnecessary once failure occurs
questions.correctAnswer: Pastoral ministry requires love and involves restoration after failure
questions.explanation: Both John 21:15 and 21:17 show Jesus thrice asking Peter if he loves Him and commanding him to feed His sheep, restoring Peter after his denial and emphasizing love as foundational to pastoral care.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 21:6 and John 21:11 teach about the nature of miraculous provision and divine abundance?
options: Divine provision surpasses natural limits and is abundant without failure
Miracles are symbolic and not meant for real provision
Provision is strictly proportional to human effort
Miraculous provision is always insufficient and fragile
questions.correctAnswer: Divine provision surpasses natural limits and is abundant without failure
questions.explanation: John 21:6 and 21:11 describe a miraculous catch of fish so abundant the net did not break, illustrating God’s abundant provision beyond natural constraints.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about Christ’s resurrection witness and apostolic testimony is taught in John 21:24-25?
options: The eyewitness testimony of the beloved disciple affirms the truth and completeness of Christ’s works
The gospel accounts are mostly legendary and lack eyewitness basis
The beloved disciple’s testimony is unreliable and secondary
John denies the reliability of his own testimony
questions.correctAnswer: The eyewitness testimony of the beloved disciple affirms the truth and completeness of Christ’s works
questions.explanation: John 21:24-25 states that the beloved disciple’s testimony is true and that the works of Jesus are too many to be fully written, affirming apostolic eyewitness authority.

questions.question: Skeptics claim the miraculous catch of fish is a later addition to the Gospel and not historical. What does John 21:1-11 actually teach about this event?
options: It describes a real post-resurrection appearance with a miraculous provision confirming Jesus’ identity
It is a purely symbolic story with no historical basis
It was a parable about fishing and not an actual event
It contradicts other resurrection appearances showing no miracles
questions.correctAnswer: It describes a real post-resurrection appearance with a miraculous provision confirming Jesus’ identity
questions.explanation: John 21:1-11 narrates a concrete event where Jesus appears to the disciples, performs a miracle of provision, and is recognized as the Lord, underscoring historicity and theological significance.

questions.question: What doctrine about the exclusivity of Christ’s lordship and call to follow is taught in John 21:19?
options: Peter’s call to follow Jesus demonstrates the exclusive lordship and call to discipleship
Anyone can follow any teacher; there is no unique call
Peter’s future death is unrelated to his discipleship
Jesus’ call to follow is optional and without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: Peter’s call to follow Jesus demonstrates the exclusive lordship and call to discipleship
questions.explanation: John 21:19 commands Peter to follow Jesus, indicating the exclusive nature of Christ’s lordship and personal call to discipleship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Jesus’ repeated questioning of Peter’s love in John 21:16?
questions.explanation: Jesus’ threefold questioning of Peter’s love in John 21:16 shows patience and willingness to restore despite previous failure, exemplifying divine longsuffering.

questions.question: How does John 21:20-23 contribute to the narrative arc concerning individual destiny and the kingdom of God?
options: It emphasizes that individual destiny is known by Christ and not for others to judge
It promises immortality to select disciples without exception
It reveals that all disciples will die in the same manner
It encourages speculation about others’ futures as central to discipleship
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes that individual destiny is known by Christ and not for others to judge
questions.explanation: Jesus’ response to Peter in John 21:22-23 stresses that knowledge of another’s destiny belongs to Christ alone, focusing disciples on their own calling.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about human weakness and divine restoration is taught in John 21:7 and John 21:15?
options: Human failure is met with divine restoration and renewed commission
Human failure results in permanent rejection by Christ
Peter’s impulsive actions are condemned without hope of restoration
Divine restoration depends on human perfection
questions.correctAnswer: Human failure is met with divine restoration and renewed commission
questions.explanation: John 21:7 shows Peter’s impulsive act after recognizing Jesus, and John 21:15 shows Jesus restoring Peter with a pastoral commission, demonstrating grace after failure.
